summary.text: One of the three Moirai; Hesiod first makes her a fatherless daughter of Nyx, then later a daughter of Zeus and Themis.
One of the three Fates born to Zeus and Themis.
One of the three Parcae, daughter of Night and Erebus, who foretold that the newborn Meleager would be noble.

story.text: In Hesiod's first genealogy, Clotho and her sisters Lachesis and Atropos are fatherless daughters of Night. They give mortals good and evil at birth and pursue the transgressions of gods and men until the offender is punished.
Later in the same poem, Hesiod makes the three Fates daughters of Zeus and Themis, sisters of the Horae, and says that Zeus gave them the greatest honor.
Apollodorus follows the Zeus-and-Themis genealogy, listing Clotho with Lachesis and Atropos among their children.
Hyginus instead makes the Parcae children of Night and Erebus. At the birth of Meleager, Clotho declared that the child would be noble before her sisters added their own portions to his fate.
